title: Sowing beetroot microgreens
subtitle: How to prepare and sow a beetroot microgreen tray, including an optional pre-soak
excerpt: Beetroot seed is a corky multi-germ cluster with a slow-absorbing outer coat. An optional 4 to 6 hour pre-soak speeds up germination significantly. After soaking (or without), rub the clusters to partially separate them, scatter at 20 to 25 g per tray, press, and blackout.
sourceNotes: UMass Extension microgreens guides (open-access). Cornell Cooperative Extension indoor growing material. Standard microgreen-growing practice synthesised from extension service material.

glossaryTerms.definition: A seed structure where multiple seeds are fused together in a corky outer layer. Beetroot and chard both produce multi-germ clusters; when sown, each cluster can germinate as a group, producing several shoots in close proximity. Partially separating the cluster before sowing gives more even distribution across the tray.

The period immediately after sowing when a second tray is stacked on top, blocking light from the sown tray. In darkness, germinating seeds direct energy into pushing the shoot upward rather than greening. For beetroot, expect three to four days in the blackout phase.

content.text: Beetroot microgreen sowing has two preparation options. Without preparation, the corky seed cluster is slow to absorb moisture and germination can take 5 to 7 days. With a short pre-soak (4 to 6 hours) and a light cluster separation step, germination happens in 3 to 4 days and coverage is more even. The soak is optional but recommended.
One 25 cm × 25 cm growing tray. A second tray for the blackout cover. Seed compost. Beetroot seed: 20 to 25 g per tray. A bowl for soaking (optional). A flat piece of card for pressing.

Optional pre-soak (recommended): soak beetroot seed clusters in a bowl of room-temperature water for 4 to 6 hours. Do not soak overnight; overly soaked beetroot seed can lose viability. The clusters absorb water and soften.

: whether soaked or dry, rub the beetroot seed clusters lightly between your palms to partially break them apart before scattering. This distributes the potential germination points more evenly across the tray.
Step 1: if soaked, drain and rinse the clusters before proceeding.
Step 2: pre-dampen seed compost and fill the tray to within 1 cm of the rim. Level the surface.
Step 3: scatter the rubbed clusters at 20 to 25 g per tray, distributing evenly across the surface in sections.
Step 4: press the clusters into firm contact with the medium.
: cover with the second tray and a light weight. Expect three to four days with pre-soaked seed, or five to seven days without a pre-soak, before shoots are upright and ready to move to light.

attrs.heading: Troubleshooting
attrs.intro: Common sowing-stage problems with beetroot microgreens.

items.symptom: Very slow germination — no shoots after day 7
items.cause: Dry outer hull not softened, or room too cold.
items.fix: Use the pre-soak option on the next attempt. Confirm room temperature is above 16°C.

items.symptom: Clustered germination with large bare patches between
items.cause: Seed clusters not separated before sowing.
items.fix: Rub the clusters more firmly before scattering. Even partial separation gives better coverage across the tray.
